title: The Most Underrated Way to Make $50K/Month
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast

stated_problem.quote: If you can't take it, who can we call?
stated_problem.speaker: Matt

idea.name: Junk removal and hauling
idea.one_liner: Remove unwanted items for homeowners and property contacts, charging by the job or load and earning additional revenue from salvage.
idea.customer: Homeowners, property owners, realtors, and other local property contacts.
idea.offer: Haul away unwanted items and dispose of them; the business also resells usable items and scraps metal.
idea.revenue_model: Job or load fees, plus resale of usable furniture and scrap metal.

I did a free post on there in the labor section and I got a phone call from a realtor.
we hit up every single real estate office in Sonoma County and dropped off candy dishes, introduced ourselves, gave them business cards, and let them know what we did.
So, I got over 2,000 realtors that I'm friends with right now, and I would say we have a big percentage of them that use us on like monthly.
In our first year, we did $87,000 part-time and our profit margin 70% because I wasn't paying for labor, nothing like that.
So, right now we're doing 50 grand a month and we're doing about 35% net.
So, most of my leads are coming from a lot of repeat business, a lot from Google business profile and mainly Facebook.

acquisition_channels.details: A free Craigslist labor-section post generated the first call.
Visited real estate offices, storage facilities, apartment complexes, senior-living facilities, open houses, and other potential referral partners.
Realtors, movers, maid services, handymen, and other contacts referred or exchanged work.
Posted in local Facebook groups and on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and YouTube; added local realtors on Facebook and shared job photos and business stories.
Later used Facebook boosts and Facebook ads.
Built a website, worked on SEO, and used Google Business Profile and local map-pack rankings.
Placed signs at busy intersections and near funeral homes, apartments, and storage units.
